## Module 19: Quality Improvement, Supervision, and Workload

| Q | Stem | Keyed answer | Explanation | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A count falls from 10 to 5 with no denominators. What does this prove? | Neither a rate improvement nor causation by itself | Best: without denominators you cannot compute a rate. Why not the others: they overinterpret a count. |  |
| 2 | What should a workload estimate include? | Direct work, follow-up, documentation, meetings, travel, and cover | Best: all the hours the work generates. Why not the others: incomplete or nonexistent. |  |
| 3 | What does a meaningful quality measure include? | Numerator, denominator, period, data source, and relevant exclusions | Best: definitions make a measure interpretable. Why not the others: incomplete or a privacy breach. |  |
| 4 | What does a balancing measure check? | Unintended effects of a change, such as added travel burden for patients | Best: improvements can cause harm elsewhere. Why not the others: they do not measure side effects. |  |
| 5 | Ten of 12 eligible referrals have a confirmed outcome. What is the rate? | 83.3% | Best: 10 ÷ 12 × 100 = 83.3%. Why not the others: inverted or wrong arithmetic. |  |
| 6 | What is the rate when the numerator and denominator are both zero? | Not calculable | Best: division by zero has no answer. Why not the others: they invent a value. |  |
| 7 | Why should social workers not be ranked by pesos raised? | Money raised depends on agency budgets and patient need, and ranking rewards chasing money over care | Best: the measure is driven by factors outside the worker’s control. Why not the others: they give the wrong reason. |  |
| 8 | What can a run chart show? | Change over time, but not its cause | Best: other changes could explain a shift. Why not the others: they overclaim. |  |
| 9 | You have no supervision four months into a new post. What should you do? | Arrange regular supervision in writing, through the department head, a peer, or a professional network | Best: supervision is part of safe practice. Why not the others: they leave you unsupported. |  |
| 10 | What is the best way to respond to chronic unpaid overtime? | Estimate the workload in hours and report the shortfall in writing with the risks | Best: make the shortfall visible to those who can fix it. Why not the others: they hide or shift the risk. |  |

## Module 20: Integrated Case Conference and Readiness for Practice

| Q | Stem | Keyed answer | Explanation | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | In an integrated case, what sets the priority? | Immediate safety and clinical urgency, then the person’s needs and goals | Best: safety first, then person-centered needs. Why not the others: they follow paperwork or convenience. |  |
| 2 | How should a case conference end? | With actions, owners, the patient’s choices, and review points | Best: decisions must be owned and dated. Why not the others: they leave nothing done or breach privacy. |  |
| 3 | A learner passes the written check but misses an urgent safeguarding escalation. What follows? | Remediation and reassessment before completion | Best: a safety failure cannot be averaged away. Why not the others: they ignore the failure. |  |
| 4 | What does the Academy completion record show? | That the program’s educational requirements were completed under its rules | Best: it is a learning record only. Why not the others: it confers no license, accreditation, or authority. |  |
| 5 | How should a five-minute case presentation open? | With the person’s own goal, in their words | Best: the person’s goal anchors the discussion. Why not the others: they bury or replace it. |  |
| 6 | What should end a case presentation? | Specific requests to named professionals, with dates | Best: specific requests get decisions. Why not the others: they produce nothing actionable. |  |
| 7 | Why keep one integrated plan instead of separate notes per domain? | So plans do not contradict each other and a colleague can act quickly | Best: integration prevents conflicting actions. Why not the others: they give the wrong reason. |  |
| 8 | Which task is outside a renal social worker’s scope even after this course? | Diagnosing psychiatric illness | Best: diagnosis belongs to mental health clinicians. Why not the others: those are core social work tasks. |  |
| 9 | Who judges your readiness for independent practice? | Your supervisor, from observed practice | Best: readiness is judged from watched performance. Why not the others: they are not valid judges. |  |
| 10 | What makes a development plan useful? | Concrete goals, methods, evidence, and dates, reviewed with the supervisor | Best: a reviewable plan shows what is done and what is not. Why not the others: they cannot be checked. |  |

# Pediatric Dialysis Nurse

## Module 1: The Pediatric Dialysis Nurse: Role, Scope and the Child&rsquo;s Journey

| Q | Stem | Keyed answer | Explanation | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | What does a Philippine nursing license, by itself, authorize? | The practice of nursing, including care of children and families | The license is the first layer. Modality training, facility authorization and privileges sit on top of it. |  |
| 2 | A nurse is authorized for adult hemodialysis. May she run a child’s treatment on pediatric lines? | Only with facility authorization for that device and age band | Authorization is by modality, device and age or size band. |  |
| 3 | The review behind this track found which pediatric-specific Philippine requirement? | None specific; facility authorization carries the weight | No separate pediatric license or ratio was found. Facility authorization therefore matters more. |  |
| 4 | Who owns the target weight for a child on hemodialysis? | The pediatric nephrologist | The nurse measures and reports; the nephrologist sets the target. |  |
| 5 | Who writes the feeding plan for a child on PD? | The renal dietitian | The nurse measures, reinforces and reports intake and growth. |  |
| 6 | In the IPPN registry, what was the overall probability of death after three years on maintenance PD? | About 5% | 5% overall, from 2% in North America to 9% in Eastern Europe. |  |
| 7 | What explained about half of the regional difference in IPPN mortality? | Country income | Income category explained 50.1% of the variance. The finding is observational. |  |
| 8 | Why does this track call the pediatric nurse a teacher as well as a clinician? | Caregivers do much of the care at home and the child will take over later | Family members and, later, the young person carry the care day to day. |  |
| 9 | When is the safest moment to say “I am not authorized for this”? | Before connection, in one clear sentence | Speaking before connection protects the child and is easier than stopping later. |  |
| 10 | Which item belongs in a learning agreement? | Supervision level by task and a review date | It fixes limits and supervision in writing. |  |
| 11 | A new pediatric dialysis nurse should usually start with which children? | Older, larger, stable children | Small infants need separate sign-off because margins are smallest. |  |
| 12 | Where are a nurse’s competency records kept? | In the facility’s approved system | The Academy is self-study and never records competence. |  |
| 13 | A question arises and you do not know who owns it. What is the default? | Ask the nephrologist first | A misrouted question costs time; an unasked one can harm. |  |
| 14 | What do the European registry and IPPN findings imply for nurses? | Systems matter, and reliable nursing is part of the system | Both are observational, but they point to resources and reliability. |  |
| 15 | Which stage usually follows dialysis for a child? | Transplant, then transition to adult care | Most children are prepared for transplant; transition follows in adolescence. |  |

## Module 2: Why Children&rsquo;s Kidneys Fail, and How a Modality Is Chosen

| Q | Stem | Keyed answer | Explanation | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Which causes predominate in younger children starting kidney replacement therapy? | CAKUT and hereditary disease | The global registry analysis found CAKUT and hereditary disease predominate in young children. |  |
| 2 | In Southeast Asia, which cause was most common in the 2026 registry analysis? | Immune-mediated glomerulopathy | Immune-mediated glomerular disease was most common in Southeast Asia. |  |
| 3 | A 3-year-old with dysplastic kidneys soaks diapers hourly. Why is water restriction risky? | He may be polyuric and salt-losing and become dehydrated | Volume and clearance are different jobs. |  |
| 4 | A polyuric child can still need dialysis because: | The kidney cannot concentrate potassium, phosphate, acid and waste | Dilute urine carries little waste. |  |
| 5 | The bedside CKiD equation uses: | Height and serum creatinine | eGFR = 0.413 × height (cm) ÷ creatinine (mg/dL). |  |
| 6 | Height 120 cm, creatinine 2.0 mg/dL. Bedside CKiD eGFR is about: | 25 | 0.413 × 120 ÷ 2.0 ≈ 24.8 mL/min/1.73 m². |  |
| 7 | Why does CKD cause poor growth? | Acidosis, bone-mineral disturbance, anemia, uremia and poor intake act together | Several failing kidney jobs converge on growth. |  |
| 8 | Why is PD often chosen for infants? | It avoids needles and blood loss, works at home and preserves veins | These are the usual reasons; the choice is individual. |  |
| 9 | Which factor leans toward hemodialysis? | Previous major abdominal surgery or ostomies | PD needs a usable peritoneum. |  |
| 10 | What is a preemptive transplant? | A transplant before dialysis starts | It avoids dialysis when a donor and the child are ready. |  |
| 11 | The pediatric automated PD benefit pilot was extended to: | July 31, 2026 | Status after July 31, 2026 was not verified; confirm before advising a family. |  |
| 12 | A mother asks which modality is better. The nurse should: | Explain what each option asks of the family and pass the choice to the nephrologist and family | The nurse informs; the family and nephrologist decide. |  |
| 13 | In the Philippine pediatric leptospirosis series, PD was started in about what share of oliguric children? | 36% | 19 of 53 oliguric children (36%). |  |
| 14 | Why must height be measured accurately? | Pediatric eGFR and growth assessment depend on it | Bedside CKiD uses height directly. |  |
| 15 | In what share of children worldwide was the cause of kidney failure unknown? | 14% | 14% overall, highest in Northeast Asia. |  |

| Q | Stem | Keyed answer | Explanation | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Whom do you introduce yourself to first? | The child, at eye level | Speaking to the child first shows respect and lowers fear. |  |
| 2 | Which is a false choice? | “Do you want to be connected now?” when it must happen | It invites a refusal you cannot honor. |  |
| 3 | What best helps a toddler during a procedure? | Short honest words just before the step and a comfort object | Toddlers live in the present. |  |
| 4 | What matters most to most adolescents? | Privacy, body image and a say in decisions | Private time and shared decisions build trust. |  |
| 5 | In the Philippines, who gives informed consent for a 9-year-old’s dialysis? | A parent or legal guardian | Minors are under 18; the child’s assent is still sought. |  |

| 7 | A child refuses the line care. First step if it is safe to pause? | Find out what the fear is | Often one step is the problem and can be changed. |  |

| 9 | Which is a safeguarding concern? | Bruises in a pattern with an explanation that does not fit | Pattern and mismatch are warning signs. |  |
| 10 | What is the nurse’s duty when abuse is suspected? | Notice, record exactly and report through the facility pathway | Trained staff assess; the nurse reports. |  |
| 11 | A child asks you to keep a secret about home. You should: | Not promise secrecy; explain that you may need to tell people who can help | Promising secrecy may trap you and the child. |  |

| 13 | Health information under the Data Privacy Act is: | Sensitive personal information | Share only with those who need it for care. |  |
| 14 | A chronically ill 12-year-old regresses during a painful step. This means: | Development is not fixed; assess the child on the day | Illness and fear move children up and down the ladder. |  |

## Module 4: Assessment, Fluid Balance and Weight-Based Arithmetic

| Q | Stem | Keyed answer | Explanation | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A 10-kg child: 200 g scale error is what share of body weight? | 2% | 0.2 ÷ 10 = 2%. |  |
| 2 | Why record whether the abdomen contains PD fluid when weighing? | Intraperitoneal fluid adds weight that is not body water gain | 600 mL in the abdomen adds about 0.6 kg. |  |
| 3 | Which measures length in a child under 2 years? | A length board | Infants are measured lying on a length board. |  |
| 4 | A cuff that is too small: | Reads falsely high | Overestimation can trigger unneeded fluid removal. |  |
| 5 | Recommended cuff bladder width is at least what share of arm circumference? | 40% | Length 80%–100% of the circumference. |  |
| 6 | 300 mL over 3 hours in a 20-kg child equals: | 100 mL/h, 5 mL/kg/h | 300 ÷ 3 = 100; 100 ÷ 20 = 5. |  |
| 7 | The calculation is correct. What follows? | Check it against the order and the child’s clinical state | Arithmetic and clinical appropriateness are separate checks. |  |
| 8 | What makes a double check independent? | The second nurse calculates without seeing your answer | Seeing an answer biases agreement. |  |
| 9 | Ten 5 mL flushes in a 10-kg child equal: | 5 mL/kg | 50 mL ÷ 10 kg = 5 mL/kg. |  |
| 10 | Net removal for a completed PD exchange is: | Drained volume minus instilled volume | Record the initial drain separately. |  |

| 13 | Why does fatigue matter in caregiver training? | Fear and fatigue block learning | Short sessions help. |  |
| 14 | A new connector type is introduced. You: | Retrain and reassess | Equipment changes are triggers. |  |
| 15 | Who helps with transport costs and respite? | The social worker | Refer early. |  |

## Module 19: Adolescence, School, Transplant and Transition

| Q | Stem | Keyed answer | Explanation | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Missed sessions in adolescence usually reflect: | Reasons such as school, embarrassment, mood, family or cost | Ask why before telling what. |  |
| 2 | Private time with an adolescent should start with: | An explanation of confidentiality and its limits | Trust needs clarity. |  |
| 3 | “I can’t keep living like this” should prompt: | A calm, direct question about mood and self-harm and escalation per protocol | Take hopelessness seriously. |  |
| 4 | A school letter needs: | Consent, plain-language condition, precautions and when to call | Share only what the school needs. |  |
| 5 | A PD catheter or fistula changes: | How a child plays | Activity with the team’s precautions. |  |
| 6 | Why complete vaccinations before transplant? | Some live vaccines cannot be given after transplant | Immunosuppression changes vaccine safety. |  |
| 7 | Which PhilHealth issuance covers post-kidney-transplant services in children? | Circular 2025-0011 | Confirm current terms. |  |
| 8 | The ISN/IPNA transition statement is: | A consensus statement | It asks for locally appropriate practice. |  |
| 9 | Transition is best judged by: | Self-management skills and stability | Skills, not birthdays. |  |
| 10 | Transfer is: | The single event of moving to the adult service | Transition is the process. |  |
| 11 | Early transition skills include: | Naming the condition and medicines, answering questions | Start simple. |  |
| 12 | A safe transfer includes: | A written summary, a named adult contact and confirmation of the first adult visit | Close the loop. |  |
| 13 | Children with CAKUT may need before transplant: | Bladder and urological assessment | Abnormal drainage can harm a new kidney. |  |
| 14 | Who evaluates a living donor? | The transplant team, separately | Donor care is separate. |  |
| 15 | Transfer timing should consider: | Readiness and stability, not only age | Avoid transferring in a crisis. |  |

## Module 20: Philippine Requirements, Records, Quality and Capstone

| Q | Stem | Keyed answer | Explanation | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Which body governs the nurse’s license? | The PRC and Board of Nursing | Each issuer governs one door. |  |
| 2 | DOH AO 2012-0001 governs: | Licensing of dialysis facilities | Facility license and standards. |  |
| 3 | Which issuance covers the pediatric automated PD pilot extension? | PhilHealth Advisory 2026-0013 | Extended to July 31, 2026; later status unverified. |  |
| 4 | Health data under the Data Privacy Act are: | Sensitive personal information | Share only for care in approved systems. |  |
| 5 | Why record delivered as well as prescribed treatment? | The gap shows what actually happened and what to fix | Records must tell the truth. |  |
| 6 | How is a record error corrected? | Correct per policy with date, time and initials | Never erase. |  |
| 7 | 4 episodes over 90 patient-months equals: | 0.53 per patient-year | 90 ÷ 12 = 7.5; 4 ÷ 7.5. |  |
| 8 | The ISPD 2024 pediatric peritonitis benchmark is: | 0.4 or fewer per patient-year | Not graded. |  |
| 9 | SCOPE reported HD catheter infections per: | 100 patient-months | Use time at risk. |  |
| 10 | In a program of eight children, a rise from 2 to 4 episodes: | Can arise from chance and case mix and needs investigation | Small denominators. |  |
| 11 | Infection rates should not be used to: | Rank individual nurses with small numbers | Interpret with case mix. |  |
| 12 | An improvement aim must be: | Specific, measurable, with a date | So you can tell if it worked. |  |
| 13 | Completing the Academy track gives: | An educational record only | Authorization is the facility’s. |  |
| 14 | A record that matches the order perfectly every time should be: | Questioned | Real care varies. |  |
| 15 | Why save the version and date of each rule you rely on? | Rules change, and pilots expire | Check issuer and date. |  |
